cs.label: [section] Cíl předmětu a studijní výstupy:
cs.content: Tento předmět odkrývá principy zakládání, pěstění a obnovy lesních porostů v kontextu různých ekologických, ekonomických a sociálních požadavků společnosti. Studenti pochopí v širokém pojetí koncept pěstování lesa a jeho využití v lesním hospodářství pro produkci dřevní hmoty i mimoprodukčních užitků lesa ve vztahu k biodiverzitě, hydrické a půdoochranné funkci lesa, rekreačního potenciálu atd.

Lectures (allowance 28/0)

en.label: a.
en.content: Purpose of the course, purpose of silviculture, forest structure, forest forms, the silvicultural system, control of stand structure process, kinds of silviculture treatments, methods of reproduction, harvesting methods, environmental consideration, world forests, science and technology in selected areas, harvesting and processing of wood products, challenges

en.label: b.
en.content: Silviculture as applied ecology, tree and its environment (solar radiation, temperature, humidity, wind, soil), site index, site quality, physiological processes (photosynthesis, respiration, transpiration), biotic relations, tree and its importance in landscape

en.label: c.
en.content: Global change -- principles, impacts on tree physiology and morphology, current and future impacts on forests, Carbon forestry - tree growth and carbon allocation, brief overview of economic aspects in silviculture

en.label: d.
en.content: Natural forests-- temperate and boreal biomes, small and large developmental cycle, theories development, identification and characteristics of developmental stages and phases, which outcomes of natural forests dynamics can we use in the silviculture and why

en.label: e.
en.content: Close to nature silviculture, concept, justification, plus and minus / historical context / current silvicultural trends / stand conversion - silvicultural methods, position of natural regeneration in the silviculture -- plus and minus / fructification of trees / seeds production, fall and distribution / conditions for germination and growth of seedlings / silvicultural methods / natural regeneration -- specifications by tree species

en.label: f.
en.content: Artificial regeneration - site preparation, seed production and nursery practice, seedling quality, containers, substrates, fertilizers, nursery and plant hygiene, nursery environment and facilities, nursery management

en.label: g.
en.content: Commercial silviculture, management for maximum volume production (spruce, pine, beech, oak), all-aged management vs. even aged management, , thinning, effect of thinning on forest stand, principles of thinning for main forest tree species (Norway spruce, European beech, Oak, mixtures), thinning models, thinning of substitute tree species stands

en.label: h.
en.content: Sustained-yield management, management of substitute tree species stands and their calssification, forests on former agricultural land, afforestation, even-aged management vs uneven-aged management

en.label: i.
en.content: Silviculture of mixed forests

en.label: j.
en.content: Selection forests, silviculture of fir, coppice, definition of selection method, forms of selection forest, structure of selection forest, Liocourt's concept, the control method of forest management, examples of selection forests in Europe -- Couvet (Switzerland), Zalesina (Croatia), Characteristics and requirements for the regeneration of silver fir and silviculture, extension of fir in Europe, Backman's growth law. Natural regeneration of silver fir - potential problems and causes, temporal and spatial regulation of natural regeneration, artificial regeneration, use of fir in transformation, silviculture of fir

en.label: k.
en.content: Mountain forest under subsiding air pollution load, main features of the mountain forest, fundamental knowledge of the forest behavior under the impact of air pollution, common differentiation frameworks for forest management, air pollution load as a crucial differentiation framework for decision making, ecological conditions on the deforested areas in exposed zones, two strategies of forest management under air pollution load, forest disintegration and natural succession, general objective of spruce forest management system, the consequences of prior air pollution effects on forest

en.label: l.
en.content: Agroforestry, fast growing tree species -- forest plantations, silviculture of pioneer tree species

en.label: m.
en.content: Treatments of introduced tree species, introduction, what is introduction, types and ways of introduction, reasons for introduction, advantages, disadvantages, possibly risks, requirement and goals of successful introduction, important introduced tree species in the Czech republic, important introduced tree species in the world
Excercise - Seminar paper preparation and presentation (allowance 0/28)

en.content: Seminar paper content deals with answers to the following questions: What is the history of silviculture in your country?What are the natural conditions for plant growth in your country?What are the dominant tree species in your forests and what are their ecological demands for optimal growth? What are the main principles of silvic in your forests?

en.label: b.
en.content: Choose one main problem in forestry of your country and present your opinion to solve it. /use literature/

en.label: c.
en.content: Reading of articles.

en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: This course will cover the principles for establishing, tending, and regenerating stands in the context of various ecological, economic, and social considerations. Students will develop a broad understanding of the silvicultural concepts and applications needed to manage forest stands for a variety of commodity and non-commodity values. Some of the values to be addressed in this course include timber production, wildlife habitat, water quality, recreation, forest health, and ecosystem restoration.
